description: Multi-dimensional adversarial review of a diff or capability: correctness, security, and spec compliance, with every finding adversarially verified before it is reported.

args.scope: Phase 7 global release review of the backend (release-review-api), part c: practice module
args.focus: This is the once-per-release whole-history review; slice reviews already happened per slice, so prioritise CROSS-MODULE and cross-slice defects. This run covers ONLY: src/main/kotlin/cz/doucko/practice (read other modules only for context at call sites). Requirements: contract/docs/requirements.md; ownership table in contract/docs/mvp-capability-plan.md; API in contract/api/openapi.yaml. Check especially: answer keys leaking to child endpoints before reveal (FR-27, NFR-1); admin endpoints reachable without the admin; any user input producing a raw 500 or driver internals (RFC 7807 required); UNPARSEABLE consuming an attempt (FR-22); attempts persisted immediately (FR-31); XP ledger never reduced (FR-38); Europe/Prague week boundaries in stats; module boundaries (Spring Modulith); migrations append-only and consistent with entities; concurrency (double submit, races on attempts/XP); path traversal / upload limits in storage; no secrets committed; tools never addressing the owner's compose project 'doucko'. Skip tests unless they mask a defect.

findings.title: Login-free problem-report endpoint has no dedupe or rate limit, so the report queue can grow without bound
findings.evidence: `report()` inserts a new `problem_report` row on every call (`store.insertReport(ReportRecord(UUID.randomUUID(), ...))`). Child endpoints need no login, and the table is append-only: there is no unique constraint on (task, attempt, status) and no throttle. Repeated POSTs, whether from a buggy client retry or from a hostile LAN client, grow the table forever and flood the admin flag queue. `listReports` returns everything unpaginated.
findings.suggestion: Collapse duplicate OPEN reports for the same task and attempt (idempotent insert, or a partial unique index on (task_id, attempt_id, reason) WHERE status='OPEN'). Consider paging `listReports`, or add a simple per-IP/per-task rate limit.

findings.title: Statistics read the entire attempt and hint history on every request
findings.evidence: `stats()` calls `store.allAttempts()` and `store.allHints()`, which load every row (including the parsed JSONB `parts` and the re-evaluation join). It then groups them in memory, even though only the last `weeks` weeks are returned. `metricMet` additionally needs only the last 5 weeks. The cost grows linearly with total history for each admin page load.
findings.suggestion: Add a store query bounded by `created_at >= start of the oldest requested week` (at least the last 5 weeks for the metric). Session splitting needs a small look-back before that boundary. The per-topic first-try counts can be computed in SQL or from primary-scope attempts only.

findings.title: Replay attempts count toward sessions, the weekly metric and reveal counts
findings.evidence: `sessions()` and `weeks()` take `store.allAttempts()` of every scope. A replay attempt (`replay=true`, which earns no XP) therefore counts as an answered task in a session. It can also push a session past `QUALIFYING_TASKS`, which feeds `metricMet`. The reveal tally `attemptNo == MAX_ATTEMPTS && !it.correct` counts replay reveals too. The KDoc states 'all scopes' deliberately, so this may be intended. The success metric is about practice habit rather than new content, so re-playing solved missions could satisfy the 4-weeks x 3-qualifying-sessions metric without new learning.
findings.suggestion: Confirm against the progress-stats spec's session definition. If replays should not count toward the metric, filter `!it.replay` in `metricMet`, or at least in the qualifying-session count. If they should, document it next to the metric.

findings.title: Duplicated RFC 7807 advice code in the child and admin practice advices
findings.evidence: `AdminStatsProblemAdvice` and `PracticeProblemAdvice` each define identical private `invalid(request, errors)` and `respond(request, status, key, customize)` helpers. They also repeat the same handlers for `PracticeNotFound`, `PracticeConflict`, `InvalidPracticeInput` and `MethodArgumentTypeMismatchException`. A fix to one, such as a missing message key or a changed `errors` shape, can silently diverge from the other.
findings.suggestion: Extract a shared package-private helper (a small class or extension taking `ProblemResponses` and `MessageSource`) that builds the field-error problem. Keep only the per-controller title keys in the two advices.

findings.title: Conflict-detail lookup throws NoSuchMessageException (raw 500) if a PracticeConflict code has no catalog entry
findings.evidence: The handler builds the detail with `messages.getMessage("practice.conflict.${exception.code}", null, request.locale)`, with no default message. The key is derived from a free-form string passed to `PracticeConflict("...")`. All six codes in use currently exist in `messages.properties`, which I verified. A new code added without a matching property line, or a typo, would turn a 409 into a 500 inside the advice itself. The same applies to `practice.error.${it.code}` in `invalid()`.
findings.suggestion: Use the `getMessage(code, args, defaultMessage, locale)` overload with the generic problem detail as default. Alternatively make the conflict code an enum so the set of keys is closed and covered by a test.

findings.title: NUL (\u0000) in a child report note or answer can reach Postgres and cause a raw 500
findings.evidence: The child can send `{"reason":"OTHER","note":"a\u0000b"}` to POST /api/child/missions/{m}/tasks/{t}/reports. ReportRules.validate only trims and counts code points, and the note is bound into the `problem_report.note` text column (JdbcPracticeStore.insertReport:123). Postgres rejects NUL in text with SQLSTATE 22021. Answers have the same risk: raw strings, including a choice key like "\u0000", are written into the jsonb `parts` array in insertAttempt:103, and jsonb rejects \u0000. Neither the checker nor the readers filter control characters (no isISOControl check found in src/main). The only practice advices handle NotFound, Conflict, Invalid, Unreadable and TooLarge, so the DataAccessException falls through to the generic handler as a 500. That breaks the AGENTS.md rule that no user input may produce a raw 500. I did not confirm that the checker returns WRONG rather than UNPARSEABLE for an answer containing NUL, so the answer path is unverified.
findings.suggestion: Reject or strip U+0000 in PracticeReaders.answers (strings and array elements) and ReportRules.note, and return a 400 with a catalog message. Also add a fallback DataAccessException handler that returns RFC 7807. Add a regression test with `\u0000` in a note and in an answer.

findings.title: Unthrottled child problem-report inserts: no rate limit or cap on rows per task
findings.evidence: The child POST /reports endpoint is unauthenticated and the child chain has CSRF disabled. Each call inserts a new OPEN `problem_report` row (up to 1000 code points of note) with no per-task or per-attempt dedupe and no cap. Any LAN host can script thousands of requests, bloating the flag queue and the table. `usedTasks` also treats every report as usage, so the task's FR-56 delete guard blocks deletion for good. Neither the schema nor the service has a uniqueness or count limit. Impact is limited by the LAN-only exposure.
findings.suggestion: Allow at most one OPEN report per (task, attempt) in the service, or add a unique partial index on that pair. Optionally add a small global cap or rate limit on child writes.

findings.title: Checklist areas reviewed in the practice module with no defect found
findings.evidence: Clean areas: (1) FR-27/NFR-1: revealed answers are produced only by DeterministicTutor when the state is REVEALED. PartView carries no answer spec, and the choice options expose only key and text. (2) FR-22: the Grade.Unreadable branch returns before store.insertAttempt, so nothing is stored. (3) FR-31: attempts are inserted inside the submit transaction under the pg advisory lock. The unique index (task_id, scope, attempt_no) also guards against a double submit. (4) FR-38: `xp_award` has a trigger refusing UPDATE and DELETE, and reevaluation XP is clamped with maxOf(0, …). (5) Europe/Prague: PragueWeeks uses ZoneId Europe/Prague with previousOrSame(MONDAY). (6) SQL: all values are bound parameters and there is no string interpolation of input; the only concatenated fragments are constants. (7) Admin endpoints (/api/admin/stats and /api/admin/reports/**) fall under the /api/admin/ admin chain. (8) Child bodies are capped at 16 KB and only `answers`, `reason`, `note` and `rankIndex` are read, so there is no mass assignment. (9) Problem responses never quote submitted values. (10) Migrations V4–V6 are append-only and consistent with the JDBC columns. (11) No secrets or PII found in the module. Dependencies and compose exposure were out of scope for this part.

findings.title: Published-mission bonus is paid by a synchronous listener inside the content publisher's transaction
findings.evidence: `onPublishedMissionChanged` uses plain `@EventListener` with `@Transactional`, so it joins the publisher's transaction. It calls `store.lock()` and then inserts into the XP ledger. A ledger failure, such as a unique-index race on `xp_award_bonus_once_uq`, would roll back the admin's publish or edit of the mission and surface through the content module's error handling. I read only the practice module, not the publishing call site.
findings.suggestion: Confirm with an integration test that a ledger failure cannot turn an admin publish into a raw 500. If it can, handle the failure or switch to `@TransactionalEventListener(AFTER_COMMIT)` with a new transaction. The startup `reconcile()` already repairs missed bonuses.

findings.title: Startup reconcile and the publish listener back-date nothing: bonus rows are stamped with Instant.now()
findings.evidence: `reconcile()` and `onPublishedMissionChanged` insert `MISSION_BONUS` rows with `Instant.now()`, and `reconcile()` inserts no celebration. A rank crossed this way is surfaced only through `HqView.pendingRankUp`. This is documented in the KDoc and does not break FR-38, because the ledger is append-only and the DB trigger refuses update and delete. The 'XP earned' figure on a mission summary is computed from `ledger.awards()` filtered by the run's attempt ids. Bonuses with a null `attempt_id` are therefore probably left out of the summary's `xpEarned`.
findings.suggestion: Add an IT that publishes a complete mission, then fetches `getMissionSummary`, and asserts the summary's XP against the ledger. If the bonus is missing from `xpEarned`, amend the spec or `RunXp.summarize`.

findings.title: Retry limit and reveal logic exist in more than one place (service, tutor, stats)
findings.evidence: The reveal count in `StatsRules.weeks` uses `attemptNo == TaskProgress.MAX_ATTEMPTS && !it.correct`. `DeterministicTutor` reveals on `state == REVEALED`. `Gamification.summary` also uses `TaskProgress.MAX_ATTEMPTS`. The contract's `maxAttempts` is mapped separately as the constant `TaskView.MaxAttempts._2`. They agree today (2), but nothing ties them together.
findings.suggestion: Derive `maxAttempts` in `PracticeMapping.task` from `TaskProgress.MAX_ATTEMPTS`, or add a test asserting they are equal.

findings.title: Verified clean: the checklist items I audited showed no defect
findings.evidence:
- **Answer keys (FR-27, NFR-1):** keys appear only through `DeterministicTutor`, and only when the state is `REVEALED`. The reload path (`screen` → `outcome`) goes through the same tutor.
- **UNPARSEABLE (FR-22):** `PracticeService.submit` returns `Grade.Unreadable` without calling `store.insertAttempt`, so no attempt is consumed.
- **FR-31:** `insertAttempt` runs inside the transaction, after `store.lock()` (an advisory transaction lock).
- **Double submit:** state is re-read under the lock, and `attempt_task_scope_no_uq` backs it up.
- **FR-38:** V5 has a trigger that refuses UPDATE and DELETE on `xp_award`. `onReevaluation` clamps with `maxOf(0, …)`. Unique indexes cover once-per-task, once-per-mission bonus and once-per-report.
- **Admin access:** `/api/admin/**` is covered by the admin security chain (`AdminSecurityConfiguration`). Only the sign-in POST is `permitAll`, and `AdminStatsController` has no auth bypass.
- **Week boundaries:** `PragueWeeks` uses `ZoneId Europe/Prague` with Monday as week start.
- **Problem responses:** `PracticeProblemAdvice` and `AdminStatsProblemAdvice` return RFC 7807 problems with catalog messages and never quote submitted values.
- **SQL:** all values are bound parameters.
I did not verify the spec scenarios one by one, `tasks.md` ticks, the OpenAPI field match, or the Modulith `verify()` boundary. I ran out of budget and did not run the tests.
findings.suggestion: No action. Run `npm run qa:verify` and `npx openspec doctor` to confirm the unaudited items.

findings.title: Mission summary first-try count ignores tasks first resolved through another mission
findings.evidence: `firstTry = attempts.count { it.attemptNo == 1 && it.effectiveCorrect && it.missionId == mission.missionId }` is divided by `mission.taskIds.size`. In the primary scope a task is shared by every mission that contains it (OQ-15). A task first answered correctly through mission A has an attempt with missionId=A. Mission B's summary then leaves it out of the numerator but keeps it in the denominator, so the child sees e.g. 2/5 although all 5 were first-try. I read the code only and did not run it against a scenario.
findings.suggestion: Check the spec for `MissionSummary.firstTryCount`. If it means first-try tasks of this mission's task list, drop the `missionId` filter for the primary scope. If the per-run semantics are intended, document that and make `taskCount` consistent.

findings.title: Client-supplied answer keys are echoed in problem `errors[].field`
findings.evidence: `FieldError("answers.$key", "unknown-part")` uses the raw JSON property name from the request. `PracticeProblemAdvice` writes it into `errors[].field`. The advice's KDoc says problems 'never quote a submitted value (NFR-3)'. Keys can be up to about 16 KB of arbitrary text. Only the requester sees it, so the risk is low, but the NFR-3 claim does not hold.
findings.suggestion: Report unknown keys as a generic `answers` field. Or truncate and escape the key, and only echo keys that match the task's part-key pattern.

findings.title: Unauthenticated child report endpoint has no volume or attempt-count limit
findings.evidence: `report()` inserts a `problem_report` row on every call, up to 1000 code points of note each. Child endpoints are login-free by design and there is no dedupe or cap per task or attempt. A script or a stuck client retry loop can flood the admin flag queue. `FlagQueue.list` loads and maps the whole queue with no paging.
findings.suggestion: Dedupe an identical OPEN report per (task, attempt, reason), or cap OPEN reports per task. Page the admin queue.

result.reasoning: The literal facts are right. `PracticeService.report()` inserts a new `problem_report` row on every call (PracticeService.kt:211), and I found no dedupe or rate limit in the code I searched. But this is a hardening wish, not a correctness defect. FR-30 says a problem report is stored with the latest attempt attached, and the code does that. Nothing in the code or the project rules requires collapsing duplicate reports. This is a single-family tutoring app on a LAN, and the child endpoints are deliberately login-free. A repeat report can be a legitimate new signal, for example a different reason or note on the same task, so collapsing on (task, attempt) could lose information. The claimed harm needs a hostile LAN client or a buggy retry loop, and the finding offers no evidence of either. A grown queue is an operational annoyance, not wrong behaviour. The finding itself rates its confidence as low. I did not check the unpaginated `listReports` claim or FR-30's exact wording. I can't positively confirm a wrong mechanism, so I'm defaulting to refuted.

The mechanism is confirmed. `PracticeService.report()` inserts a new `problem_report` row on every call. The V4 migration has no unique constraint beyond the `id` primary key. The only other index on the table is the non-unique `problem_report_task_idx` on `task_id`, and V6 adds the non-unique queue index `problem_report_queue_idx`. I found no dedupe or rate limit in the code I read. I did not open the web layer or the security config, and I did not check `listReports` for pagination. An unauthenticated caller who has a valid mission id and task id can therefore repeat the POST and add rows each time. The practical impact is small. This is a single-family LAN app with login-free child endpoints by design, and the caller needs valid UUIDs. The worst case is a noisy admin queue and some table growth, not data exposure or corruption. The finding is real but low-impact, so the existing "minor" severity and low confidence are about right.

The code does what the finding says. `stats()` calls `allAttempts()` and `allHints()`, and both are unbounded SELECTs (JdbcPracticeStore.kt:181-191). But this is a scalability concern, not a correctness defect, and the finding is filed under the correctness dimension. The results are correct, and the class doc states the whole-log design on purpose: "weekly figures from the whole attempt log". The per-topic first-try counts need the full primary-scope history anyway, because they come from the first play-through. So the suggested time bound would not work for that part without a separate query. The app serves one child plus an admin page, so linear growth in history is negligible in practice. I can't confirm a wrong mechanism, so I'm refuting it as a correctness finding. At most it is an optional optimization note.

The mechanism is real. stats() calls the unbounded store.allAttempts() and store.allHints() (ProgressStats.kt:67,78; JdbcPracticeStore.kt:181,187) and groups them in memory, so cost grows linearly with history on each admin stats load. The impact is negligible: the app has a single child user, the endpoint is admin-only and read-only, an attacker can't trigger it, and the design deliberately computes stats from the whole log. The per-topic first-try counts also genuinely need full primary-scope history, so part of the suggestion is invalid. Only the weekly and metric computations could be bounded. I didn't measure row counts.

The behavior is exactly what the spec requires, so it is not a defect. The progress-stats spec (openspec/specs/progress-stats/spec.md:11-13) says sessions "SHALL be built from every logged attempt of every run (replays included)". `revealed` counts "the second wrong attempts by their week", with no replay exclusion. `Stats.kt` `sessions()`, `weeks()` and the reveal filter match this. The KDoc "all scopes" is deliberate. The finding itself says it may be intended and only speculates about the metric. It names no spec deviation. The suggested fix, filtering `!it.replay`, would contradict the spec. The remaining point, documenting the choice next to `metricMet`, is a style nit and not a correctness bug.

Counting replay attempts toward sessions, weekly figures and reveals is deliberate. design.md for implement-progress-stats-api (line 39) states sessions use every logged attempt of every scope, including replay runs. StatsRulesTest pins it (`replay attempts count towards sessions and answered tasks`, line 163; `replay hints and reveals count in their week`, line 279). OQ-14 defines a session as answered tasks with no gap over 30 minutes and does not exclude replays. OQ-17 and FR-33 withhold only XP and the bonus from replays. Replaying is still practice, which is what the success metric measures. No attacker or real-user harm exists: it's a LAN-only family app and the metric is parent-facing. The finding's confidence is low and it concedes the behaviour may be intended. I couldn't run `openspec show` for the store spec text because Bash was disabled, so the conclusion rests on the design doc, the tests and the requirements.

The cited code matches the finding. The finding doesn't hold up as an exploitable or reproducible problem. The lookup key `practice.conflict.${exception.code}` is built only from hard-coded string literals at the six `PracticeConflict(...)` call sites: resolved, no-hint, replay-not-complete, summary-not-complete, report-not-open and report-no-attempt. The listener is synchronous and joins the publisher's transaction. That is a real property of the code, but it is deliberate, and the claimed failure does not occur. `onPublishedMissionChanged` calls `store.lock()` first, which is `pg_advisory_xact_lock` on a fixed key (JdbcPracticeStore:36). `reconcile()` takes the same lock, and `onReevaluation` documents that its caller holds it. Every bonus writer therefore runs one at a time. The "already paid?" check (`bonusesPaid`) and the insert happen under the lock. Postgres READ COMMITTED gives each statement a fresh snapshot, so after the lock is acquired the check sees any bonus committed by a concurrent writer. A competing insert can't slip in between the check and the insert, so `xp_award_bonus_once_uq` can't be hit. The unique index is a backstop only. The publisher also holds `lock.exclusive()`, a separate advisory lock, but that doesn't change this. The only remaining way for the ledger insert to fail is a general database fault, and that would break the publish transaction anyway. Same-transaction behavior is also the intended design (OQ-28: the bonus is earned "now", atomic with the publish). Switching to AFTER_COMMIT would risk a missed bonus on publish. The finding's own confidence is low, and it admits it did not read the call site.

rejected.title: Published-mission bonus is paid by a synchronous listener inside the content publisher's transaction
rejected.evidence: `onPublishedMissionChanged` uses plain `@EventListener` with `@Transactional`, so it joins the publisher's transaction. It calls `store.lock()` and then inserts into the XP ledger. A ledger failure, such as a unique-index race on `xp_award_bonus_once_uq`, would roll back the admin's publish or edit of the mission and surface through the content module's error handling. I read only the practice module, not the publishing call site.
rejected.suggestion: Confirm with an integration test that a ledger failure cannot turn an admin publish into a raw 500. If it can, handle the failure or switch to `@TransactionalEventListener(AFTER_COMMIT)` with a new transaction. The startup `reconcile()` already repairs missed bonuses.
verifierNotes: The listener is synchronous and joins the publisher's transaction. That is a real property of the code, but it is deliberate, and the claimed failure does not occur. `onPublishedMissionChanged` calls `store.lock()` first, which is `pg_advisory_xact_lock` on a fixed key (JdbcPracticeStore:36). `reconcile()` takes the same lock, and `onReevaluation` documents that its caller holds it. Every bonus writer therefore runs one at a time. The "already paid?" check (`bonusesPaid`) and the insert happen under the lock. Postgres READ COMMITTED gives each statement a fresh snapshot, so after the lock is acquired the check sees any bonus committed by a concurrent writer. A competing insert can't slip in between the check and the insert, so `xp_award_bonus_once_uq` can't be hit. The unique index is a backstop only. The publisher also holds `lock.exclusive()`, a separate advisory lock, but that doesn't change this. The only remaining way for the ledger insert to fail is a general database fault, and that would break the publish transaction anyway. Same-transaction behavior is also the intended design (OQ-28: the bonus is earned "now", atomic with the publish). Switching to AFTER_COMMIT would risk a missed bonus on publish. The finding's own confidence is low, and it admits it did not read the call site.

The synchronous, transaction-joining listener is real. MissionService publishes PublishedMissionChanged inline and Gamification uses a plain @EventListener with @Transactional. But the failure the finding describes can't be reproduced. The listener first takes a transaction-scoped Postgres advisory lock (`pg_advisory_xact_lock`, JdbcPracticeStore.lock). Only then does it check `bonusesPaid` and insert. A concurrent writer therefore waits until the other transaction commits and then sees the bonus as paid. That is the same serialization the attempt path uses, so the `xp_award_bonus_once_uq` race is guarded. The remaining failures are infrastructure errors such as a DB outage, which would fail the publish regardless. The coupling is also deliberate: OQ-28 says the bonus is credited at publish time. The suggested AFTER_COMMIT alternative would add a different failure mode, where the bonus is missed until the next startup reconcile. This is not an exploitable bug, and there is no path for an attacker or user to trigger it.
